doc.title: yq: -p json without --slurp streams concatenated top-level values, succinctly parses one document
doc.body:
**Severity: Medium**

## Summary

Discovered while implementing #2778's scalar-grammar validation for `-p json`/`--input-format json`. Real yq's JSON front end (`goccy/go-json` via `-p json`, no `--slurp`/`--eval-all`) reads a *stream* of concatenated top-level JSON values from stdin — matching `jq`'s traditional multi-document-on-stdin behavior — and applies the filter to each value independently. `succinctly yq --input-format json` (no `--slurp`) always parses the entire input as exactly one document/value; it has no concept of reading multiple top-level values from a single stream.

## Repro

Captured live against Homebrew `yq` v4.53.3:

```console
$ printf '1 2' | yq -p json -o=json -I=0 '.'
1
2
$ printf '1 2' | succinctly yq --input-format json -o=json -I=0 '.'
"1 2"

$ printf 'true: 1' | yq -p json -o=json -I=0 '.'
true
1
$ printf 'true: 1' | succinctly yq --input-format json -o=json -I=0 '.'
{"true":1}

$ printf '"a": 1' | yq -p json -o=json -I=0 '.'
"a"
1
$ printf '"a": 1' | succinctly yq --input-format json -o=json -I=0 '.'
{"a":1}
```

Note the separator between streamed values is surprisingly lenient in the real decoder — plain whitespace (`1 2`), and even `:` (`true: 1`, `"a": 1`) all work as a "separator," which reads like `json.NewDecoder(...).Decode()` called repeatedly in a loop, each call consuming exactly one JSON value and leaving the rest of the stream for the next call, with no validation of what sits *between* values beyond finding the next legal value-start byte.

## Root cause / mechanism

`succinctly yq --input-format json` routes through `YamlIndex::build_json_sourced` → `Parser::json_strict`, a single-document parser (`src/yaml/parser.rs`). There is no loop anywhere in the non-`--slurp` path that re-invokes parsing after a value completes to pick up trailing content as a second value — trailing content is either silently absorbed into the current parse (pre-#2778 behavior for shapes like `true: 1`, read as a YAML mapping) or, after #2778, may be rejected outright depending on what follows.

## Why this is separate from #2778

#2778's scope is scalar-*grammar* validation within an otherwise single-document JSON-sourced parse (rejecting `True`/`.5`/`+1`/etc., and structural tokens with no JSON spelling like `?`/`&`/`!`). This issue is about *stream* semantics — how many top-level values a single `-p json` invocation reads at all, which is an orthogonal, more architectural gap. #2778 initially attempted a "bare `key: value` is always invalid" rejection that turned out to be wrong precisely because of this streaming behavior (`"a": 1`/`true: 1` are valid, complete two-value streams in real yq) — that rejection was reverted rather than landing a new divergence, deferring the real fix to this issue.

## Suggested fix direction

Not investigated in depth. A `--slurp`-like internal loop for the non-`--slurp` `-p json` path — parse one JSON value, note the resulting text length, skip acceptable separator whitespace, and if input remains, parse another value, filtering/emitting each independently the way `jq`'s own default multi-document stdin handling does — would need scoping against `evaluate_yaml_direct_filtered`/`yq_runner.rs`'s existing single-document assumptions, which run deep (the M2 fast path, output formatting, `-0`/`--indent` handling all currently assume one document per run for this route). Likely Tier 3 (architectural) given the blast radius across the evaluator, not a narrow parser fix.

doc.title: yq: {$a} inside object construction should silently produce zero output, matching real yq's COLLECT_OBJECT quirk
doc.body:
## Summary

Follow-up from #2724. That issue fixed jq mode's `{$a}` object-construction
shorthand (and the `{$a: expr}` dynamic-key form). yq mode was deliberately
left untouched there -- it still raises the same pre-existing parse error
it always has ("expected identifier, found '$'") -- because real yq's
actual behavior for this shape is a third, unrelated thing: not an error,
and not jq's `{"a":1}` either.

## What real yq actually does

```console
$ printf 'x: 1\n' | yq '1 as $a | {$a}'
$ echo $?
0
```

Empty stdout, exit 0. `--verbose` shows why: yq's `{...}` object-
construction grammar has **no shorthand concept at all** -- confirmed
separately that even the plain (non-`$`) field shorthand is rejected
outright at the lexer level:

```console
$ printf 'x: 1\n' | yq '{x}'
Error: 1:2: lexer: invalid input text "x}"
```

So `{$a}` isn't sugar in real yq -- it's `$a` (an ordinary `GET_VARIABLE`
op) evaluated as a bare, non-`key: value` entry inside `COLLECT_OBJECT`.
The verbose log shows `COLLECT_OBJECT` degrading on an odd/unpaired input:
`"collectObjectOperation, length of rotated is 0"` -> `"PROCESSING
VARIABLE DONE, got back: 0"` -> `"no matching results, nothing to
print"`. It's an incidental quirk of yq's object-collection operator
handling a non-pair entry, not a deliberate feature.

## Why this is separate from #2724

Reproducing this needs new **evaluator**-level behavior (an object-
construction entry that consumes zero pairs and yields nothing), not a
parser change -- #2724's fix was purely parse-time desugaring. It also
interacts with a pre-existing, already-shipped (and separately
undocumented) succinctly extension: succinctly's yq mode *already* accepts
the plain `{x}` shorthand as sugar for `{x: .x}`, which is itself a
divergence from real yq's lexer-level rejection shown above -- so there
are now two separate open questions about how far yq mode's object-
construction sugar should extend past real yq's much stricter grammar,
not one.

## Suggested next step

1. Decide the target: reproduce real yq's exact "bare non-pair entry
   degrades the whole construction to zero output" behavior (ADR-0018's
   preferred bug-for-bug default), or make a documented, deliberate call to
   keep succinctly's existing shorthand-sugar convenience extension and
   accept the divergence (recording it in
   `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`, which currently has no entry for
   object-construction shorthand of any kind despite the plain `{x}` case
   already existing and diverging).
2. Whichever is chosen, also close the parallel gap for the plain `{x}`
   shorthand noted above -- it's the same question, just discovered a level
   up.

comments.author: newhoggy
comments.body:
## Triage plan (2026-09-12)

**Premise check on current `main` (2581b17c9):** still reproduces, and the gap is wider than the issue states. Re-probed against yq v4.53.3 and `./target/release/succinctly yq`:

```console
$ printf 'x: 1\n' | yq '1 as $a | {$a}'            # (empty, exit 0)
$ printf 'x: 1\n' | succinctly yq '1 as $a | {$a}' # Error: parse error at position 11: expected identifier, found '$'
$ printf 'x: 1\n' | yq '{x}'                       # Error: 1:2: lexer: invalid input text "x}"
$ printf 'x: 1\n' | succinctly yq '{x}'            # x: 1
$ yq -n '{b: 2}'                                   # Error: 1:2: lexer: invalid input text "b: 2}"   <-- bare identifier KEYS are a lexer error too
$ succinctly yq -n '{b: 2}'                        # b: 2
```

Real yq's `{...}` grammar is `{ expr : expr , expr : expr , ... }` where **both** key and value are ordinary expressions (`{1: 2}` -> `1: 2`, `{.a: 5}` on `{"a":1}` -> `1: 5`, `{"a" | "b": 1}` -> `b: 1`, `"k" as $a | {$a: 3}` -> `k: 3`), `:` is the binary `CREATE_MAP` op, `,` is `UNION`, and the braces are `COLLECT_OBJECT`. A bare identifier is simply not a token. succinctly yq mode currently accepts jq's identifier-key grammar (`{b: 2}`, `{x}`) and rejects every non-identifier/non-string/non-paren key (`{$a: 3}`, `{1: 2}`, `{.a: 5}`, `{1 as $k | $k: 2}` all "expected identifier").

Bare (non-pair) entries are fully characterised by `collectObjectOperator` in `pkg/yqlib/operator_collect_object.go` (fetched v4.53.3 source into scratch; mechanism verified live against every row below):

| filter (`yq -n`) | real yq | why |
|---|---|---|
| `1 as $a \| {$a}` / `{"k"}` / `{.x}` / `{[1,2]}` | empty, exit 0 | scalar/seq first entry: `N = len(first.Content)` drives the loop; scalar N=0 -> nothing; seq `[1,2]` N=2 but splatting scalars yields nothing |
| `{$undefined}` / `{$__doc}` | `{}` | undefined var yields *no* results, union empty -> "starting with empty map" |
| `{$__doc, "z": 9}` | `z: 9` | ditto; first surviving entry is the pair |
| `{"b", "a": 1}` / `{"a":1} \| {.a, "z": 9}` | empty | first entry scalar -> N=0 |
| `{"a": 1, "b"}` / `{"z": (1,2), 5}` / `{"a":1} as $a \| {$a, "b": 2}` | `Error: CollectObject: mismatching node sizes; are you creating a map with mismatching key value pairs?` | later entry has fewer children than `first.Content` |
| `[[{"k":1}]] as $a \| {$a}` | `k: 1` | seq-of-seq-of-map is exactly the shape `CREATE_MAP` emits, so it collects normally |
| `[{"k":1}] as $a \| {$a}` | `1` | splat of a map yields its values |
| `{"k":{"x":1}} as $a \| {$a}` | `1` | a map's `Content` is the flat `[key, value]` list: N=2, rotated[0]=`"k"` (scalar, splats to nothing), rotated[1]=`{x:1}` splats to `1` |
| `[["k",1]] as $a \| {$a}` | `k` then `1` | splat of a seq yields its items |
| `[{"k":1}] as $a \| {"z": 0, $a}` | `Error: cannot multiply !!map with !!int` | cross-multiply `{z:0} * 1` |

`CREATE_MAP` (`operator_create_map.go`) emits, per input matching node, a flow seq of one-key maps (key x value cross product), wrapped in an outer seq (one element per matching node); `COLLECT_OBJECT` then takes `N = len(first.Content)`, errors on any result with fewer children, and for each `i` folds `rotated[i]` with `collect`: splat each candidate (seq -> items, map -> values, scalar -> nothing), first non-empty splat seeds the accumulator, every later one is cross-multiplied in via `multiply` (the same `*` merge used by `*=`, `AppendArrays: false`).

No open PR references #2783. A limitations entry already exists (`docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md` § "Object-construction shorthand (`{x}`, `{$a}`) has no real-yq equivalent at all (#2783)") but it records only `{x}`/`{$a}`, not the bare-identifier-key gap or the key-expression gap.

**Root cause / mechanism:** `Parser::parse_object_construction` (`src/jq/parser.rs`) uses jq's grammar for both modes: key = `(expr)` | `"string"` | (jq only) `$name` | identifier; missing `:` = field shorthand. yq mode has no branch for an arbitrary key expression and no notion of a bare entry, so anything else dies in `parse_ident`'s "expected identifier" error. Evaluation (`build_object_entries` in `src/jq/eval.rs`, `build_object_entries_generic` in `src/jq/eval_generic.rs`) is a pure key x value cross product over `ObjectEntry { key: ObjectKey, value: Expr }` -- there is no representation for a non-pair entry, and no `COLLECT_OBJECT` collapse/mismatch logic.

**Plan:**

Decision under ADR-0018 (#2416 decision order), applied per sub-case:

- Bare identifier keys and `{x}` shorthand: real yq *rejects the syntax at the lexer*, so the #1512 amendment governs -- yq mode must match the rejection by default and keep succinctly's jq-style sugar only behind `--jq-extensions` (same shape as `reject_unless_jq_extensions`). Nothing in rule 4 lets us refuse a lexer error; "users like `{b: 2}`" is not a listed condition.
- `{$a}` / bare entries / expression keys / `mismatching node sizes` error: real yq accepts these, rule 3 (bug-for-bug) applies, reproduce the `COLLECT_OBJECT` mechanism.

1. **Parser** (`parse_object_construction`, `src/jq/parser.rs`): in `ParserMode::Yq` (without `--jq-extensions`) parse each entry as `key_or_bare = parse_pipe_no_comma_with_booleans()`; if the next char is `:`, parse the value at the same level and push a pair; otherwise push a bare entry. Keep the existing `"string"` / `(expr)` / identifier / `$name` branches for jq mode and for yq-with-`--jq-extensions` (that flag keeps today's `{x}`/`{b: 2}` acceptance, so no `--jq-extensions` user loses anything). Error message for the default-mode identifier case should reuse the `reject_unless_jq_extensions_at`-style text so it is discoverable ("bare identifier keys are not part of yq's syntax; quote the key or pass --jq-extensions"). Note `{$__loc__: 1}`'s jq-only compile error stays jq-only.
2. **AST** (`src/jq/expr.rs`): add a bare form. Cheapest option that keeps every existing `ObjectEntry` match arm compiling: `ObjectKey::Bare` with the expression in `value` (then every `ObjectKey` match needs an arm) -- or a separate `Expr::Object { entries, yq_collect: bool }`. Check `Expr` size pins first (memory: any new field on `Expr` costs +8 bytes and there is a size-pin test) -- putting the discriminant on `ObjectKey`, not `Expr`, avoids that. Sweep every `Expr::Object`/`ObjectKey` consumer: `needs_path_context`, `owned_to_expr_at_depth`, the #2135 depth accounting, `collect_call_sites`, `is_constant`-style predicates (`git grep -n "ObjectKey::" src/`).
3. **Evaluators** (both `build_object_entries` in `src/jq/eval.rs` and `build_object_entries_generic` in `src/jq/eval_generic.rs` -- memory: two separate evaluators, both need the change). Fast path unchanged: when no entry is bare and the mode is jq, or every entry is a pair in yq mode, today's cross product is byte-identical to yq's `COLLECT_OBJECT` for a single input, keep it. Slow path (yq mode, any bare entry): a new `collect_object_yq(entries, input) -> Result<Vec<OwnedValue>>` helper on `OwnedValue` that literally implements `collectObjectOperator`: evaluate entries in order into a union list where a pair entry contributes one `Seq[Seq[one-key maps]]` and a bare entry contributes its raw outputs; `N = child count of first` (map = 2*len, seq = len, scalar = 0); mismatch -> `Error("CollectObject: mismatching node sizes; are you creating a map with mismatching key value pairs?")`; per-`i` fold with splat + `*` merge (reuse the existing yq-mode multiply used by `*=`, `MergeFlags::default()`), including its `cannot multiply !!map with !!int` error text. Union empty -> single `{}`.
4. Confirm the `needs_path_context`/path-register interaction: a bare entry is never a path expression; the object-construction result already "resets the path context", so the slow path can return plain values.
5. **Tests:** pin the whole table above as oracle captures in `tests/yq_cli_tests.rs` (default mode) plus the `--jq-extensions` counterparts (`{x}` -> `x: 1`, `{b: 2}` -> `b: 2`, `{$a}` -> `a: 1` with the flag on, mirroring jq mode). Add a `jq`-mode must-not-change sweep for `{$a}`, `{$a: expr}`, `{x}`, `{"a": 1, "b"}` (jq: `{"a":1,"b":null}`) so the shared code does not regress jq. Parser unit tests for the new yq branch (`{1: 2}`, `{.a: 5}`, `{"a" | "b": 1}`, `{1 as $k | $k: 2}`). Then run the whole suite: ~18 yq-mode CLI tests and an unknown number of `eval.rs` yq-mode tests use bare-identifier keys and must be re-pointed at quoted keys (or `--jq-extensions`), each after checking the yq golden fixtures do not already cover the case.
6. **Docs:** rewrite the existing #2783 section in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md` -- move `{x}`/`{b: 2}` to the § Extensions list under `--jq-extensions` (they are rule-5 gated extensions now, not divergences) and record the residual divergence: non-string keys (`{"k":1} as $a | {$a: 3}` renders a complex `? k: 1\n: 3` key in real yq; succinctly should error there since `OwnedValue` object keys are strings). Update `docs/reference/yq-language.md` gated-builtins section and the CLAUDE.md `--jq-extensions` mention.

**Risks / open questions:**
- Rejecting `{b: 2}` by default in yq mode is user-visible; it is exactly what #1512 did for fifteen builtins, but the owner may want it called out in the release notes. The `--jq-extensions` escape keeps the old behaviour available.
- Multi-input semantics: with `-n`/single document `N` is always 1 for pair entries; under `eval-all`/`.[] |` fan-in real yq's `N` equals the number of matching nodes and the result is one object per input (`yq ea '{"x": .a, "y": .a}'` gives per-doc objects), which succinctly's per-value evaluation already produces. A bare entry whose child count differs from the input count (`yq ea '[.[] | .a] as $v | {"x": .a, $v}'` -> mismatch error) is the one place the two models diverge; pin it if `ea` is supported, otherwise note it.
- Complex (non-string) keys from expression keys are out of scope; error and record.
- Precedence of the new key expression: `parse_pipe_no_comma_with_booleans` is the #2506 level already used for values; confirm `{"a" | "b": 1}` and `{1 as $k | $k: 2}` parse the same way (both verified accepted by real yq above).

**Dependencies / related:** #2724 (jq-mode fix, done), #1512 (`--jq-extensions` gate precedent), #2506 (`and`/`or` level inside braces), ADR-0018 rule 3/5 and the #1512 amendment. No open PRs.

**Class:** Opus -- one AST shape change consumed by both evaluators (`eval.rs` and `eval_generic.rs`) plus a parser-grammar switch for yq mode, a fidelity fork that has to be resolved per sub-case under ADR-0018 (lexer-rejected sugar goes behind `--jq-extensions`; accepted shapes reproduce `COLLECT_OBJECT` bug-for-bug, including two error messages and a splat/multiply fold), and a test-suite sweep with regression risk in jq mode via shared code. Not Fable: no new ADR, no new value representation, the reference source pins the semantics exactly.

doc.title: yq: comment set-operators (head_comment=, foot_comment=, comments=, tag=) are unimplemented
doc.body:
Spun out of #798, which is being closed as an umbrella. The *read* side of yq's
comment metadata has landed (#2674 grammar, #2690 storage, #2704/#2718 capture,
#2758 getters). The *write* side is still unimplemented for three of the slots.

## What fails today

On `main` (`54658bca0`), `succinctly yq`:

```
$ printf 'a: 1\n' | succinctly yq '.a head_comment = "hi"'
Error: head_comment = ... is not yet supported
$ printf 'a: 1\n' | succinctly yq '.a foot_comment = "bye"'
Error: foot_comment = ... is not yet supported
$ printf 'a: 1\n' | succinctly yq '.a comments = "x"'
Error: comments = ... is not yet supported
$ printf 'a: 1\n' | succinctly yq '.a tag = "!!str"'
Error: tag = ... is not yet supported
```

The grammar accepts all four — `MetaSlot::{HeadComment, FootComment, Comments, Tag}`
parse fine and reach `eval_meta_assign` in `src/jq/eval.rs`, which raises from a
single explicit arm:

```rust
MetaSlot::Tag | MetaSlot::HeadComment | MetaSlot::FootComment | MetaSlot::Comments => {
    suppress_or_raise(EvalError::new(format!("{} = ... is not yet supported", ...)), optional)
}
```

`line_comment =`, `style =` and `anchor =` already work (#2674).

## What real yq does (pinned v4.53.3)

```
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: 2\n' | yq '.a head_comment = "hi"'
a: 1
# hi
b: 2

$ printf 'a: 1\nb: 2\n' | yq '.a foot_comment = "bye"'
a: 1
# bye

b: 2

$ printf 'a: 1 # old\n' | yq '.a comments = "x"'
a: 1 # x
# x

# x

$ printf 'a: 1\n' | yq '.a tag = "!!str"'
a: "1"
```

Notes from those captures:

- `comments = "x"` sets **head, line and foot together** — three separate
  emissions, not one.
- `foot_comment` emits a **blank line after** the comment; `head_comment` does not.
  (Both yq placements above look surprising relative to the key they were set on —
  reproduce them bug-for-bug per ADR-0018, do not "fix" them into what seems right.)
- `tag = "!!str"` is a **coercion**, not just metadata: the scalar is re-emitted
  quoted. That is a different mechanism from the comment slots and may deserve
  splitting out again if it turns out to be the larger half.
- yq clears a comment with the empty string: `... comments = ""` strips every
  comment in the document (`# h\na: 1 # x\nb: 2\n` → `a: 1\nb: 2\n`).

## Also missing: `...` in yq mode

The `... comments = ""` idiom above is yq's documented way to strip all comments,
and succinctly's yq-mode parser rejects the token outright:

```
$ printf 'a: 1\n' | succinctly yq '... comments = ""'
Error: parse error: parse error at position 2: unexpected character '.'
```

`...` is recursive descent including keys (jq's `..` is values only). Whether it
belongs in this issue or its own is an implementation call — it is listed here
because it is the only way to reach the clear-everything behaviour.

## Why it is blocked

The write side has no storage to write into and no emitter to print it:

1. `NodeMeta.head_foot_comment` is `Option<Box<HeadFootComment>>` and is
   hardcoded `None` at **every** construction site — notably
   `to_owned_with_comments_at_depth` in `src/jq/eval_generic.rs`. The field is
   private with no setter. (It is boxed deliberately: un-boxing it re-breaks
   `reconcile_presentation_panics_past_nesting_depth_limit_1005` by growing
   `reconcile_presentation_at_depth`'s frame past its own depth guard — see the
   #2690 history.)
2. Neither emitter prints head/foot comments at all — that is the round-trip gap
   tracked by #2795. **That issue's DOM half is
   a hard prerequisite**: until `emit_yaml_value_at_depth` can print a head/foot
   comment, a successful write would be invisible.

So the ordering is: round-trip PR B (populate `NodeMeta` + DOM emitter) first,
then this.

## Acceptance

- `.a head_comment = "hi"`, `.a foot_comment = "bye"`, `.a comments = "x"` and
  `... comments = ""` match pinned yq v4.53.3 byte-for-byte.
- `tag = "!!str"` coerces, matching yq.
- Differential fuzz against pinned yq over randomly-placed comments, not a
  hand-picked matrix — the write side is directly observable, so this is available
  here in a way it was not for #2704.
- `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`: remove the entries these close; record any
  divergence that survives.
- `omni-dev coverage diff` at 100% before pushing.

comments.author: newhoggy
comments.body:
## Triage plan (2026-09-12)

**Premise check on current `main` (2581b17c9):** still reproduces in full. All four slots raise `<slot> = ... is not yet supported` (`.a head_comment = "hi"`, `.a foot_comment = "bye"`, `.a comments = "x"`, `.a tag = "!!str"` on `a: 1\nb: 2`), `... comments = ""` is a parse error at position 2, and `line_comment =`/`style =`/`anchor =` still work. The issue's four yq captures re-verified byte-for-byte. Extra captures that shape the plan (pinned yq v4.53.3, doc `a:\n  b: 1\n  c: 2\ns:\n  - x\n  - y`):

```
.a head_comment = "h"          -> a:\n  # h\n  b: 1 ...            (container value: above its first child)
.a.b head_comment = "h"        -> a:\n  b: 1\n  # h\n  c: 2        (scalar value: printed BELOW its own line)
(.a | key) head_comment = "h"  -> # h\na: ...                      (key node: above the key line)
.a foot_comment = "f"          -> a:\n  b: 1\n  c: 2\ns:\n# f\n  - x  (column 0, between the next key and its items)
.s[0] head_comment = "h"       -> s:\n  # h\n  - x                 (item: above)
.s[1] foot_comment = "f"       -> ...  - y\n  # f                  (last item: below, no blank line)
.a comments = "m\nn"           -> a:\n  # m\n  # n\n  b: 1 ... s: # m\n\n# n\n# m\n# n\n  - x   (head+line+foot, foot gets the blank line)
... head_comment = "h"         -> writes key AND value heads: `# h\n# h\na:` at the top
.a head_comment |= . + "z"     -> Error: !!str () cannot be added to a !!map (a)   (|= binds . to the value, as line_comment does)
.a tag = "!!int" / "!!str" / "!foo" / "!!float" / ""   on a: 1  -> a: 1 / a: "1" / a: !foo 1 / a: !!float 1 / a: 1
.c tag = "!!bool" on c: yes    -> c: !!bool yes ;   .a tag = "!!str" | .a | type -> !!str
```

Two adjacent gaps found while probing, both silent no-ops on `main` (the outcome #798 ruled out): `(.a | key) line_comment = "k"` prints `a: 1` where yq prints `a: 1 # k` — the write resolver has no way to name a key node, so the candidate list is empty and the stage is skipped; and the DOM route still drops an explicit tag on a plain write (`a: !!float 1` + `.a = .a` → `a: 1.0`, yq keeps `!!float 1`), which is the same missing tag slot `tag =` would need.

**Root cause / mechanism:** `src/jq/eval.rs` `eval_meta_assign` has one explicit `not yet supported` arm for the four slots; `src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs` `WritableSlot::of` returns `None` for them so `resolve_one_meta_assign` never builds a `MetaEffect`. Three separate things are missing underneath, none of them in the evaluator:
1. **No storage or printer for head/foot on the DOM route.** `NodeMeta.head_foot_comment` (`src/jq/eval_generic.rs`) is `None` at every construction site including `to_owned_with_comments_at_depth` (the parser-side `NodeComments { head, line, foot }` and the `head_comment`/`foot_comment` getters exist, so the *cursor* has the data); `emit_yaml_value_at_depth` (`yq_runner.rs`) prints nothing for head/foot. That is exactly #2795's DOM half — PR #2825 (open) covers the *streaming* route only.
2. **No tag slot.** `NodeMeta` has `comment`/`style`/`anchor`/`head_foot_comment`; the scalar arm of `to_owned_with_comments_at_depth` consumes `explicit_tag()` for resolution and discards it, and the emitter has no tag arm (which is also why `style = "tagged"` is refused).
3. **No key-node addressing and no `...`.** `MetaPathStep` is `Key(String) | Index(usize)` — a value position only — and the yq-mode parser has no `...` token (`try_parse_meta_op`'s target grammar). `... comments = ""` needs both, and `... head_comment` shows yq writes the key *and* the value head.

**Plan** (split into three PRs/sub-issues; this issue stays as the tracker):

*PR A — `tag =` (independent of #2795):*
1. Add `tag: Option<String>` to `NodeMeta` (`from_comment_and_style` and `empty()` gain the field; watch `size_of` — the head/foot `Box` exists because `reconcile_presentation_at_depth`'s frame is depth-guard-sensitive, so re-run `reconcile_presentation_panics_past_nesting_depth_limit_1005` after widening).
2. Seed it in `to_owned_with_comments_at_depth`'s scalar arm from the cursor's `explicit_tag()` (fixes the `a: !!float 1` round-trip drop as a by-product), and add `MetaEffect::Tag(Option<String>)` / `WritableSlot::Tag` with yq's coercion rule measured above: `!!str` on a non-string re-renders quoted (mirror the existing `style = "double"` effect plus a `type` change — check `.a tag = "!!str" | .a == "1"` against yq before deciding whether the *value* is rewritten or only its rendering), a core tag that already matches the resolved type is a no-op, any other tag renders as `!tag value` (one emitter arm, which also unblocks `style = "tagged"`), `""` clears.
3. `eval_meta_assign`: route `MetaSlot::Tag` through the same `eval_update(target, identity)` path as the three working slots.

*PR B — head/foot/comments writes (after #2795's DOM half lands):*
4. Populate `NodeMeta.head_foot_comment` in `to_owned_with_comments_at_depth` from the cursor's `head_comment_raw()`/`foot_comment_raw()` for values *and* for keys (the object arm already keeps a per-key side map, `key_comment_map`; it needs a head/foot pair per key too), and have `reconcile_presentation_at_depth` carry them like it carries `key_comments`. Give `emit_yaml_value_at_depth` the placement rules measured above and in PR #2825's streaming printer (`stream_yaml_value_at`'s head/foot arms are the reference implementation to mirror: key head above the key at its indent; container-value head above its first child; scalar-value head *below* the line, bug-for-bug; foot below with one blank line when a sibling follows and none when it ends the collection). This is #2795's DOM half and should be filed/landed under that issue, not this one.
5. Then here: `MetaEffect::HeadComment/FootComment(Option<String>)` reusing `meta_comment_text`, and `Comments` expanding to the three effects on the same target; `eval_meta_assign` routes the three slots through `eval_update` identity like the others.

*PR C — key targets and `...`:*
6. Extend `MetaPathStep` with a key-node step (a resolved path ending at `key`), and teach `resolve_one_meta_assign` to produce it — today it evaluates `path(TARGET)`, which cannot express `key`; either peel a trailing `| key` off the target expression before `path()` or make `path()` in yq mode emit a key marker. This also fixes the silent `(.a | key) line_comment = "k"` no-op, so it can land before B with just `line_comment`.
7. Add `...` to the yq-mode lexer/parser (`src/jq/parser.rs`; `..` values-only vs `...` values-and-keys) and evaluate it as `..` plus, per mapping, each key node; only the meta-assign resolver needs the key half, so it can be a `Builtin::RecurseWithKeys` that `resolve_one_meta_assign` special-cases if a general key-node value is out of reach (that is #2785's territory — do not block on it).
8. Tests: goldens via `scripts/sync-yq-golden.sh` for every capture above plus `... comments = ""` on a document with head/line/foot/key comments; a differential fuzz over randomly placed `head_comment`/`foot_comment`/`comments` writes at random paths (the write side is directly observable, unlike #2704); `eval.rs` unit tests for the `eval_meta_assign` routing; a negative test that `|=` on head/foot binds `.` to the value (the `!!map` error above).
9. Docs: `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md` "Metadata assignment" entry — drop the refused-slots bullet piecewise as A/B/C land, record any surviving divergence (candidates: the `.a foot_comment` column-0 placement if it is decided to be unreadable output under ADR-0018 rule 4 — check `yq` reads its own output back first; it does for the probes above); `docs/reference/yq-language.md` for `...`.

**Risks / open questions:**
- Placement fidelity is the risk: go-yaml's emitter puts a scalar value's head *below* its line and a mapping value's foot at column 0 under the *next* key — reproduce, do not "fix" (ADR-0018 rule 3), but check each shape reads back with yq before pinning it.
- PR A's `tag = "!!str"` coercion may need the value rewritten (so `type`/`==` see a string), not just the rendering — decide from the oracle, and keep the jq-mode evaluator untouched (meta ops are yq-only).
- `NodeMeta` growth vs the #1005 depth guard (see the `Box` rationale on `head_foot_comment`).
- Whether `...` should be a general value-level builtin or a resolver-only construct depends on #2785's outcome (typed key nodes); the plan above avoids depending on it.

**Dependencies / related:** #2795 (DOM half is a hard prerequisite for PR B; streaming half in PR #2825), #798 (umbrella, closed), #2785 / PR #2804 (key nodes), #2763 (closed — getters after `key`), #747/#1132 (tag drop on the DOM route), #2811 (attribution the DOM head/foot seed will inherit), #2806 (same `to_owned_with_comments` seed point).

**Class:** Opus — kept. Each of the three pieces is a multi-site change across the parser, `eval.rs`, the generic `to_owned_with_comments` walker, `reconcile_presentation`, and the DOM emitter, with semantics that must be re-derived from the oracle over a matrix (placement per node kind, tag coercion per type) and a real design fork (how a key node is addressed by the write resolver). No new ADR or `OwnedValue` representation is needed — `NodeMeta` already is the side-table for this — so it stops short of Fable, but it must be split and sequenced as above rather than attempted as one PR.

doc.title: yq: =`'s right side still yields false for a zero-node literal/constructor operand (#2540 residual)
doc.body:
## Summary

[#2540](https://github.com/rust-works/succinctly/issues/2540) fixed `and`/`or`'s own read-only-context handling of a literal/constructor operand whose upstream pipe stage produced zero nodes (e.g. `(.a.zz | true) and true` now correctly answers `true`, matching real yq). The identical `Context.DontAutoCreate` mechanism (#2470) also applies to `=`'s right side, and it diverges the same way:

```console
$ printf 'a:\n  b: 1\nx: 5\n' | yq -o=json -I0 '.x = (.a.zz | true)'
{"a":{"b":1},"x":true}
$ printf 'a:\n  b: 1\nx: 5\n' | succinctly yq -o=json -I0 '.x = (.a.zz | true)'
{"a":{"b":1},"x":5}
```

Real yq gives `x: true`; succinctly leaves `x` unchanged (`5`).

## Why #2540 didn't cover this

`and`/`or` evaluate their operands through `jq::eval::boolean_fanout_bools`, shared by both evaluators, which is where #2540's fix (`yq_empty_context_literal_or_constructor`) was added. `=`'s right side evaluates through a completely separate mechanism (`jq::eval::yq_prepare_assign_targets`/`resolve_dynamic_indexes`), which #2540 did not touch — fixing this needs its own trace through that code path, not a second call to the same classifier from the wrong place.

## Suggested approach

Find wherever `=`'s right side currently registers "zero outputs" for the empty-context case (likely near `yq_prepare_assign_targets`'s own handling of a read-only right-side evaluation, #2470/#2481) and consult `jq::eval::yq_empty_context_literal_or_constructor` there the same way `boolean_fanout_bools` now does, before falling through to the existing "target unchanged" behavior.

## Verification notes

Re-verify the same shape matrix #2540 already established (literal, `[...]` — regardless of body, `{...}` — only when every field value also independently qualifies) against `=`'s right side specifically, since the surrounding mechanism differs even though the underlying "is this operand really empty" classification should be identical.

## Related

- #2540 (fixed `and`/`or`'s own copy of this gap)
- #2470 (the read-only context mechanism both share)
- `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`'s "An `and`/`or` operand's evaluation context" section, which already documents this residual

comments.author: newhoggy
comments.body:
## Triage plan (2026-09-12)

**Premise check on current `main` (2581b17c9):** still reproduces, and the residual is wider than "literal/constructor on `=`'s right side" — #2540's classifier is *itself* too narrow, and that shows on `and`/`or` too. Re-probed live against Homebrew yq v4.53.3 on `a: {b: 1}` / `x: 5` (`-o=json -I0`; `.a.zz` genuinely absent):

| filter                                   | yq v4.53.3        | succinctly yq       |
|------------------------------------------|-------------------|---------------------|
| `.x = (.a.zz \| true)` / `7` / `"s"` / `null` / `-1` | that value | `x: 5` (unchanged) |
| `.x = (.a.zz \| [1,2])`, `[.b]`, `[true]`, `[]` | `x: []`     | unchanged           |
| `.x = (.a.zz \| {"q": 1})`               | `x: {"q":1}`      | unchanged           |
| `.x = (.a.zz \| {"q": [1]})`             | `x: {"q":[]}`     | unchanged           |
| `.x = (.a.zz \| {"q": .b})`, `.b`, `length`, `tostring`, `. // 3`, `select(true)` | unchanged | unchanged (agree) |
| `.x = (.a.zz \| 1 + 1)`, `"s" + "t"`, `1 == 1`, `1 // 3` | `2`, `"st"`, `true`, `1` | unchanged |
| `.x = (.a.zz \| true \| not)`, `1 \| tostring`, `[1] \| length`, `{"q": 1} \| .q`, `"a" \| test("a")`, `1 \| . + 1` | `false`, `"1"`, `0`, `1`, `true`, `2` | unchanged |
| `.x = (.a.zz \| (true, false))`, `(1, .b)`, `(.b, 1)` | `false`, `1`, `1` | unchanged |
| `.x = ([.a.zz \| true])`                 | `x: [true]`       | `x: []`             |
| `.x \|= (.zz \| true)`                   | `x: true`         | unchanged           |
| `.x += (.a.zz \| 1)`                     | `x: 6`            | unchanged           |
| `.zz = (.a.zz \| true)`                  | `zz: true`        | `zz: null`          |
| `(.x, .a.b) = (.a.zz \| true)`           | both `true`       | unchanged           |
| `.x = (.a.zz \| 1) + 1`, `((.a.zz \| 1) == 1)`, `((.a.zz \| 1) // 3)` | `2`, `true`, `1` | `1`, `false`, `3` |
| `(.a.zz \| 1 + 1) and true`              | `true`            | **`false`**         |
| `(.a.zz \| false \| not) and true`, `(.a.zz \| [1] \| length) and true` | `true` | **`false`** |
| `(.a.zz \| (true, false)) and true`      | `true`, `false` (two results) | **`false`** (one) |
| `(.a.zz \| 1) + 1` (top level, read-only) | `2`              | `1`                 |

Agreeing rows: `.x = (.a[5] | true)` (`true` in both — an out-of-range index does not go empty), `.x = (.a.zz | true | . and false)` (`false`), `.x = (.a.zz | true and false)` (`false`), `.x = (1,2)` (`2`, yq's collapse-to-last). Note `{q: 1}`, `empty` and `if` are lexer errors in real yq, so they are not oracle cells.

**Root cause / mechanism:** two layers.

1. The consumer gap the issue names: `collect_rhs_outputs` (`src/jq/eval.rs`, the prologue shared by `eval_assign`/`eval_compound_assign`/`eval_alternative_assign`) enters `yq_read_only_context` (#2470) and, when the right side yields `QueryResult::None`, returns an empty vector that `normalize_rhs_values_for_fork` turns into "one document, target auto-created, never written". It never consults `yq_empty_context_literal_or_constructor` the way `empty_boolean_operand_bit` does. The generic evaluator's owned-identity pipe (`eval_generic.rs`, the `needs_path_context(stage)` branch that builds `yq_assign_rhs_document`) prefetches through the same function, so it inherits the fix.
2. The classifier gap: `yq_empty_context_literal_or_constructor` models yq's rule as "the pipe's *last* stage re-emits a static value". Real yq's model (verified from `operator_value.go`/`operator_collect.go`/`operator_create_map.go` for #2540) is per-operator: the *first* context-free stage re-emits its node(s) into an otherwise-empty context, and every later stage then runs normally on those nodes. That is why `true | not`, `[1] | length`, `1 + 1` (both operands re-emit, then add), `(true, false)` (both branches re-emit), and `(.a.zz | 1) + 1` (the operand pipe re-emits `1`) all produce values in yq. The same classifier feeds `and`/`or`, so those rows are wrong today too.

**Plan:**
1. Replace `yq_empty_context_literal_or_constructor(expr) -> Option<OwnedValue>` with `yq_empty_context_reemit(expr) -> Option<Expr>` in `src/jq/eval.rs`: return an expression that, evaluated against a `null` input inside the read-only scope, reproduces what yq emits. Rules: `Literal` → itself; `Array(_)` → the literal `[]` (regardless of body); `Object` → itself only if every key and value is itself re-emittable with no pipe remainder (keep #2540's all-or-nothing rule; `{"q": [1]}` → `{"q": []}`, so rewrite the field values too); `Comma` → the comma of the re-emittable branches, `None` if none qualify (`(1, .b)` → `1`); `Neg` → itself if its operand qualifies; `Arithmetic`/`Compare`/`And`/`Or`/`Alternative` → itself if both operands qualify (evaluated against `null`, a context-free operand tree gives the same answer as yq's re-emit); `Pipe(stages)` → find the first stage `i` that qualifies, return `Pipe([rewritten_i, stages[i+1..]...])` — the remainder runs on the seed values through the ordinary evaluator; `Paren` via `strip_parens` as today. Anything else → `None`.
2. `collect_rhs_outputs`: in the `QueryResult::None` arm (and `Partial(vs, _)` with empty `vs` only if the control is not an error — check `Break`/`Halt` ordering against #400/#494 first), consult `yq_empty_context_reemit(value_expr)` under `S::READ_ONLY_ABSENT_KEY_IS_EMPTY`; if `Some(rewritten)`, evaluate it with `eval_owned_input::<W, S>(&rewritten, &OwnedValue::Null, optional)` *inside the still-open `_scope`* and return those outputs. The existing `normalize_rhs_values_for_fork` then applies yq's collapse-to-last, which gives `(true, false)` → `false` and `(.x, .a.b) = …` its fan-out for free.
3. `empty_boolean_operand_bit` (`eval.rs`) and its twin `read_only_operand_strategy_generic` (`eval_generic.rs`): evaluate the rewritten expression instead of taking one static value, and push *every* output's truthiness bit — `(.a.zz | (true, false)) and true` must yield two results. `boolean_fanout_bools` is already the shared entry point, so wire the rewrite there once.
4. Arithmetic/comparison/alternative operands in read-only context (`eval_binary_fanout`'s empty-operand path, `empty_outer_operand_pass` and `empty_outer_operand_pass_generic`): before falling to `yq_empty_operand_output` (#2460), consult the rewrite for the empty operand — this closes `(.a.zz | 1) + 1` and `((.a.zz | 1) // 3)`. Gate on `rules.read_only` exactly like step 3; jq mode and non-read-only yq contexts are untouched (`(.a.zz | 1) + 1` at the top level already agrees because `.a.zz` auto-creates there).
5. Tests: rename/extend `test_yq_empty_context_literal_or_constructor_and_operand_2540` and `test_yq_empty_context_constructor_value_shapes_2540` in `tests/yq_cli_tests.rs` with every row of the table above for `=`, `|=`, `+=`, `and`/`or`, and the arithmetic-operand rows; keep the agreeing rows as negative controls (`{"q": .b}`, `.b`, `length`, `select(true)`, `.a[5]`). Unit tests for `yq_empty_context_reemit` in `src/jq/eval.rs` (pipe with a qualifying head and a non-qualifying tail, comma with mixed branches, object with a nested array field). A jq-mode guard row (`/usr/bin/jq '.x = (.a.zz | true)'` on the JSON twin gives `x: true` because jq's `.a.zz` is `null`, not empty — so jq mode must not enter this path at all).
6. Docs: rewrite `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`'s "An `and`/`or` operand's evaluation context — resolved for `and`/`or` (#2540); `=`'s right side remains open" section: drop the "Residual, not yet fixed" paragraph, replace the "last stage" description with the first-context-free-stage model, and extend the captured matrix with the new rows. Update `yq_empty_context_literal_or_constructor`'s doc comment (it documents the old model in detail).

**Risks / open questions:**
- The classifier is shared by `and`/`or`: widening it changes those answers too (correctly per the table, but it is a second behaviour change in one PR — call both out and pin both).
- Evaluating the rewritten expression against `null` is only sound because every stage kept in it is context-free by construction; a stage the classifier admits by mistake (`Expr::Shared` is deliberately not unwrapped today — keep it that way) would read `null` where yq reads nothing. Keep the admitted set closed and enumerate it in the doc comment.
- `Partial` with a trailing control: decide whether a `Break`/`Halt` after zero outputs still gets the re-emit (probe `.x = (.a.zz | 1, halt)`-style shapes only if yq's lexer accepts them; it rejects `empty`, so the space is small).
- Multi-target `(.x, .a.b) = …` goes through the same prologue; confirm the fork loop sees the seeded values once, not once per target.

**Dependencies / related:** #2540 (the classifier being generalised), #2470 (read-only scope), #2481 (`yq_assign_rhs_document`), #2460 (`yq_empty_operand_output`, which stays the fallback). No open PR references #2588.

**Class:** Opus — the fix is not "call the existing classifier from one more place": the classifier's model is wrong and has to be re-derived from a matrix into a rewrite-and-continue form, then wired into four consumers across both evaluators (`=` family, `and`/`or`, arithmetic/comparison operands, and the generic owned-identity prefetch). The oracle pins every cell, so no ADR or new representation is needed (not Fable), but the change reaches shared operand-emptiness machinery with real regression risk for the #2460/#2540 rows that already agree.

doc.title: yq: stages before a metadata assignment are evaluated twice, so a side effect in an assignment RHS (`.a = (.b | debug) | .a line_comment = "y"`) fires twice
doc.body:
## Summary

When a pipe contains a #798 metadata assignment (`line_comment =`, `style =`, `anchor =`), every earlier stage is evaluated twice: once by the write pass that works out which document the metadata write sees, and once by the real evaluation. A side effect inside such a stage therefore fires twice:

```
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: 2\n' | succinctly yq --jq-extensions '.a = (.b | debug) | .a line_comment = "y"'
["DEBUG:",2]
["DEBUG:",2]
a: 2 # y
b: 2
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: 2\n' | succinctly yq --jq-extensions '.a = (.b | debug) | .a = .a'
["DEBUG:",2]
a: 2
b: 2
```

Reproduced on succinctly at `3a3e88140`. Real yq has no `debug` (its lexer rejects it), so this is only reachable through `--jq-extensions`, but the duplicated output is wrong on its own terms: the control case prints once.

## Mechanism

`resolve_meta_assign_writes` (`src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs`) runs before evaluation. To make `.a = 2 | .b line_comment = (.a | tostring)` write `# 2` (as real yq does) it re-evaluates each stage preceding the last metadata write through `evaluate_input_quiet` and carries the first output forward as the document the next stage sees. `is_value_identity_stage` exempts a bare `debug`/`debug(msg)` *stage* precisely so its side effect isn't repeated, but a `debug` (or `stderr`, `input`, `halt_error`, ...) nested inside a stage's right-hand side is still re-run.

## Possible directions

- Detect a side-effecting builtin anywhere inside a stage that precedes a metadata write (a walk with `jq::walk::any_subexpr`, the way `count_meta_assigns` already does) and either refuse explicitly or fall back to resolving against the pristine document for that pipe.
- Or remove the re-evaluation entirely by applying the write *during* evaluation (`eval_meta_assign` recording `(path, slot, text)` into a thread-local the runner drains), which is also the route #2705 needs. That makes each stage run exactly once.

## Notes

- Found while reviewing the #798 PR1 branch; the pipe-sequential resolution that introduces the second evaluation was part of that review's fixes.
- `input`/`inputs` would be worse than a duplicated line (they consume input), but they are not shape-preserving so the write pass never runs for a pipe that contains them at top level; only a nested use inside an assignment RHS could reach this.

comments.body:
## Triage plan (2026-09-12)

**Premise check on current `main` (`2581b17c9`):** still reproduces, and it is wider than the issue states — it is reachable *without* `--jq-extensions`, because `stderr` and `halt_error` are not gated in yq mode (real yq's lexer rejects both: `.a = (.a | stderr)` → `lexer: invalid input text "stderr)"`, same for `halt_error`; that missing gate is a separate, unfiled gap).

```
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: 2\n' | succinctly yq --jq-extensions '.a = (.b | debug) | .a line_comment = "y"'
["DEBUG:",2]
["DEBUG:",2]
a: 2 # y
b: 2
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: 2\n' | succinctly yq --jq-extensions '.a = (.b | debug) | .a = .a'   # control
["DEBUG:",2]
a: 2
b: 2
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: 2\n' | succinctly yq '.a = (.b | stderr) | .a line_comment = "y"'      # no flag needed
22a: 2 # y
b: 2
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: 2\n' | succinctly yq '.a = (.b | halt_error) | .a line_comment = "y"'  # halts twice
2
2
[exit 1]
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: 2\n' | succinctly yq --jq-extensions '.a |= (. | debug) | .a line_comment = "y"'
["DEBUG:",1]
["DEBUG:",1]
a: 1 # y
b: 2
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: 2\n' | succinctly yq --jq-extensions '.a = 3 | select(.b | debug) | .a line_comment = "y"'
["DEBUG:",2]
["DEBUG:",2]
a: 3 # y
b: 2
```

A `debug` inside the metadata write's *own* RHS fires once today (`.a line_comment = (.b | debug | tostring)`): only the pre-pass evaluates the RHS, the real evaluation's `eval_meta_assign` ignores it. That count must not change.

**Root cause / mechanism:** `resolve_meta_assign_writes` (`src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs`) runs before `eval_with_cursor_using` and, to learn the document each `MetaAssign` stage sees, re-runs every preceding stage through `evaluate_input_quiet` (a fresh `JsonIndex` re-index + `jq::eval`), then the real evaluation runs the same stages again. `is_value_identity_stage` only skips a *bare* `debug`/`debug(msg)` stage; anything nested inside a stage (an assignment RHS, a `|=` filter, `select`'s predicate) runs twice, and `evaluate_input_quiet` swallows the pre-pass's own `Halt`/`Error` so a `halt_error` prints its payload twice before the real one exits.

**Plan (fix the mechanism, not the symptom — this is also the change #2705 needs, so it is done once, here):**

1. Move the write resolution *into* the real evaluation. Add a `pub mod meta_writes` to `src/jq/eval.rs` on the `alias_identity` pattern (thread-local + `enter() -> Guard` + `take()`, `#[cfg(feature = "std")]` with a no-op `no_std` stub like `yq_read_only_context`), holding `Vec<RecordedMetaWrite { path: Vec<MetaPathStep>, effect: MetaEffect }>`. Move `MetaPathStep`, `MetaEffect`, `WritableSlot`, `validate_style`, `RENDERABLE_STYLES`, `meta_comment_text`, `meta_anchor_name`, `plain_scalar_text` (or its caller), `meta_path_from_value`, `owned_value_at` from `yq_runner.rs` into that module — they are pure functions with no CLI dependency.
2. Extend the `Expr::MetaAssign` dispatch arm in `eval_single` (`src/jq/eval.rs`) to pass `value`/`is_update` into `eval_meta_assign`. In `eval_meta_assign`, *when a recorder is installed*: evaluate `path(TARGET)` against `input` (the document that stage actually sees — the runner's re-evaluation becomes unnecessary), evaluate the RHS exactly as `resolve_one_meta_assign` does today (`=`: `value | tostring` once against `input`, first output; `|=`: per candidate, `.` bound to the candidate's current value via `owned_value_at`, missing candidate reads `null`), validate (`validate_style`/`meta_anchor_name`), push the writes, then run the existing `TARGET |= .` value-tree step. Validation failures return `QueryResult::Error(..)` from here — that improves fidelity as a side effect: `.a style = "bogus" | error("boom")` reports `unknown style bogus` like yq (today succinctly reports `boom`, because the pre-pass is skipped when the pipe is not shape-preserving), and `.a style = "tagged" | .b` stops silently succeeding.
3. In `evaluate_yaml_cursor` (`yq_runner.rs`): install the guard around `eval_with_cursor_using` (same lifetime as `alias_identity_guard`), `take()` the writes after, and feed them to the unchanged `apply_meta_assign_writes`. Delete `resolve_meta_assign_writes`, `resolve_one_meta_assign`, `evaluate_input_quiet`, `flatten_pipe_stages`, `is_value_identity_stage`, `count_meta_assigns` and the "top-level pipe stage" refusal (its shapes now work — `as` binds by substitution in `each_as_generic`, so `$x` is already a literal by the time `eval_meta_assign` runs; #2705 covers the tests/docs for that). Keep the gate that the writes are only *applied* when `presentation_sync_ctx` exists; when the recorder holds writes but there is no ctx (the #2679 shape `.a | .b line_comment = "hi"`), report an explicit error instead of today's silent drop.
4. Ordering check: a forked evaluation (`.[] as $x | .a line_comment = $x`) records one write per fork in evaluation order and `apply_meta_assign_writes` applies them all to every result document, which is what real yq prints (two documents, both `a: 1 # 2`, captured live).
5. Tests (`tests/yq_cli_tests.rs`, `meta_assign_*_798` golden style where an oracle exists): (a) the four probes above pin "fires exactly once" for `debug` in an assignment RHS, in a `|=` filter and inside `select(...)`, plus `stderr` and `halt_error` without `--jq-extensions` (exit code unchanged, payload printed once); (b) `.a line_comment = (.b | debug | tostring)` still prints DEBUG once; (c) every existing `meta_assign_*_798` golden byte-identical; (d) `.a style = "bogus" | error("boom")` → `unknown style bogus` (oracle-captured); (e) `--inplace` test `inplace_applies_the_metadata_write_to_the_file` unchanged.
6. Docs: update the `#798 PR1` entry in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md` (mechanism paragraph names `resolve_meta_assign_writes`; drop the "top-level pipe stage" refusal bullet — #2705 owns the wording), and CLAUDE.md's #798 mention if any references the pre-pass.

**Risks / open questions:** `eval_meta_assign` must run exactly once per stage per fork — verify no retry path re-runs a completed body (`?//` alternatives and `try` only re-run on failure, which yields no output anyway, but a write recorded by a failed alternative would leak; snapshot/rollback the recorder length around `each_pattern_alternatives` if the test in step 5 shows it). `MetaPathStep` moves into the library, so `no_std` builds need the stub (run the ci.yml no_std leg). Note the deleted "top-level" refusal must not reintroduce a silent no-op: the recorder either applies or errors.

**Dependencies / related:** #2705 (same mechanism; do its residual after this lands), #2679 (silent drop of a write behind a non-shape-preserving stage — step 3 turns it into an explicit error), #798. Unfiled: `stderr`/`halt_error` are accepted in yq mode without `--jq-extensions` though real yq's lexer rejects them.

**Class:** Opus — the fix moves resolution across the library/CLI boundary (`eval.rs` bridge arm + a new thread-local module + `yq_runner.rs` pass deletion), has to reproduce the oracle's per-fork ordering and error ordering, and touches the shared `eval_single` dispatch; regression risk is moderate and only the golden suite proves it neutral.
